nodes.summary: Let $F_n$ denote the Fibonacci numbers ($F_0 = 0$, $F_1 = 1$) and, for $n \ge 0$, let $E_n$ and $O_n$ be the sums of $F_{j+1} F_{n-j+1}$ over the even and over the odd integers $j$ with $0 \le j \le n$. For every integer $k \ge 1$, $E_{2k} = O_{2k} + F_{2k+2}$.
nodes.title: Even and odd parts of the Fibonacci self-convolution at even length

nodes.summary: Let $F_n$ denote the Fibonacci numbers ($F_0 = 0$, $F_1 = 1$) and, for $n \ge 0$, let $E_n$ and $O_n$ be the sums of $F_{j+1} F_{n-j+1}$ over the even and over the odd integers $j$ with $0 \le j \le n$. For every integer $k \ge 1$, $E_{2k-1} = O_{2k-1}$.
nodes.title: Even and odd parts of the Fibonacci self-convolution agree at odd length

nodes.summary: For $n \ge 0$, $E_n$ is the rational number $\sum F_{j+1} F_{n-j+1}$, the sum taken over the even integers $j$ with $0 \le j \le n$, where $F_i$ is the $i$-th Fibonacci number ($F_0 = 0$, $F_1 = 1$).
nodes.title: Even part of the Fibonacci self-convolution

nodes.summary: For an integer $n$, $F_n$ is the $n$-th Fibonacci number as a rational number: $F_0 = 0$, $F_1 = 1$, $F_{n+2} = F_{n+1} + F_n$ for $n \ge 0$, and $F_{-n} = (-1)^{n+1} F_n$ for $n > 0$.
nodes.title: Fibonacci numbers at integer indices

nodes.summary: For $n \ge 0$, $v_n$ is the rational number $v_n = \sum_{j=0}^{n} F_{j+1} F_{n-j+1}$, where $F_i$ is the $i$-th Fibonacci number ($F_0 = 0$, $F_1 = 1$).
nodes.title: Fibonacci self-convolution

nodes.summary: Let $F_n$ denote the Fibonacci numbers ($F_0 = 0$, $F_1 = 1$) and, for $n \ge 0$, let $v_n = \sum_{j=0}^{n} F_{j+1} F_{n-j+1}$, and let $E_n$ and $O_n$ be the sums of the same terms $F_{j+1} F_{n-j+1}$ over the even and over the odd integers $j$ with $0 \le j \le n$. For every integer $k \ge 1$, $E_{2k} = (v_{2k} + F_{2k+2})/2$ and $O_{2k} = (v_{2k} - F_{2k+2})/2$.
nodes.title: Halving the Fibonacci self-convolution at even length

nodes.summary: Let $F_n$ denote the Fibonacci numbers ($F_0 = 0$, $F_1 = 1$) and, for $n \ge 0$, let $v_n = \sum_{j=0}^{n} F_{j+1} F_{n-j+1}$, and let $E_n$ and $O_n$ be the sums of the same terms $F_{j+1} F_{n-j+1}$ over the even and over the odd integers $j$ with $0 \le j \le n$. For every integer $k \ge 1$, $E_{2k-1} = v_{2k-1}/2$ and $O_{2k-1} = v_{2k-1}/2$.
nodes.title: Halving the Fibonacci self-convolution at odd length

nodes.title: Self-convolution of higher-order Fibonacci numbers

nodes.summary: Let $m \ge 1$ and let $(F_n)_{n \in \mathbb{Z}}$ be a sequence of rational numbers with $F_n = F_{n-1} + \dots + F_{n-m}$ for every integer $n$, $F_i = 0$ for $0 \le i < m - 1$ and $F_{m-1} = 1$. For $n \ge 0$ let $w_n = \sum_{j=0}^{n} F_{j+m-1} F_{n-j+m-1}$; for integers $N$, $l$ and rational $q$ let $S(N, l, q) = \sum_{k=0}^{N} q^k F_{k+l}$ and $S_2(N, l, q) = \sum_{k=0}^{N} k q^k F_{k+l}$, both equal to $0$ when…
nodes.title: Explicit formula for the shifted self-convolution of higher-order Fibonacci numbers

nodes.summary: Let $m \ge 1$ and let $(F_n)_{n \in \mathbb{Z}}$ be a sequence of rational numbers with $F_n = F_{n-1} + \dots + F_{n-m}$ for every integer $n$, $F_i = 0$ for $0 \le i < m - 1$ and $F_{m-1} = 1$, and for $n \ge 0$ let $w_n = \sum_{j=0}^{n} F_{j+m-1} F_{n-j+m-1}$. Then for every integer $n \ge 0$, $(m+1) w_{n+1} - 2m w_n = (n+m+2) F_{n+m} - (n+m) F_{n+m-1}$.
nodes.title: Recurrence for the shifted self-convolution of higher-order Fibonacci numbers

nodes.summary: For a sequence $F : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Q}$ and natural numbers $m$ and $n$, the shifted self-convolution is $w_n^{(m)} = \sum_{j=0}^{n} F_{j+m-1} F_{n-j+m-1}$, with the indices computed in the integers.
nodes.title: Shifted self-convolution

nodes.summary: A sequence $F : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Q}$ satisfies the $m$-step Fibonacci recurrence if $F_n = F_{n-1} + F_{n-2} + \dots + F_{n-m}$ for every integer $n$, that is, $F_n = \sum_{i=0}^{m-1} F_{n-i-1}$. For $m = 0$ this says $F_n = 0$ for all $n$.
nodes.title: The $m$-step Fibonacci recurrence

nodes.summary: A sequence $F : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Q}$ is the standard order-$m$ Fibonacci sequence if it satisfies the $m$-step Fibonacci recurrence, $F_i = 0$ for every natural number $i < m - 1$, and $F_{m-1} = 1$, where $m - 1$ is computed in the integers.
nodes.title: The standard order-$m$ Fibonacci sequence

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, this is the sum of $F_{j+1} F_{n-j+1}$ over the odd $j$ with $0 \le j \le n$, where $F_k$ are the Fibonacci numbers ($F_0 = 0$, $F_1 = 1$, $F_{k+2} = F_{k+1} + F_k$). It is the part of $v_n = \sum_{j=0}^{n} F_{j+1} F_{n-j+1}$ that comes from odd $j$.
nodes.title: Odd part of the Fibonacci walk count

nodes.summary: For a sequence $F : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Q}$, a natural number $m$, integers $N$ and $l$, and a rational number $q$, $S_2(m,N,l,q) = \sum_{k=0}^{N} k q^k F_{k+l}$; for $N < 0$ this is the empty sum $0$. The value does not depend on $m$.
nodes.title: First-moment weighted sum

nodes.title: Closed form for weighted sums of an $m$-step Fibonacci sequence

nodes.summary: For a sequence $F : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Q}$, a natural number $m$, integers $N$ and $l$, and a rational number $q$, $S(m,N,l,q) = \sum_{k=0}^{N} q^k F_{k+l}$; for $N < 0$ this is the empty sum $0$.
nodes.title: Weighted sum of a sequence

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
